title: Business Impact Analysis
summary: A business impact analysis is the structured study that determines how the loss or degradation of each business process, and the resources that process depends on, would affect the organisation over time. It is the analytical foundation of business continuity and disaster recovery planning because it produces the numbers that drive every later decision: the maximum tolerable period of disruption, the recovery time objective, the recovery point objective, the minimum acceptable service level and the priority order for restoration when resources are scarce. A competent analysis works process-first rather than asset-first. It starts from the organisation's products and services, breaks them into business processes, identifies the people, applications, data, facilities, suppliers and infrastructure each process needs, and then models impact across several dimensions: financial, regulatory and legal, operational, customer and reputational, and safety where relevant. Impact is assessed over a time axis because most disruption is tolerable for minutes and intolerable after days, and that curve is what makes a recovery objective defensible rather than arbitrary. Practitioners should insist on named process owners providing input, because a BIA produced solely by the security team will encode technical assumptions that no part of the business has agreed to. The output feeds continuity strategies, dependency mapping, third-party risk assessment, recovery testing scenarios and the risk register, and it should be refreshed when the business changes rather than on a fixed multi-year cycle alone.
objectives: You will be able to derive business processes and their dependencies from products and services rather than from an asset list.
You will be able to model impact across financial, regulatory, operational, customer and safety dimensions.
You will be able to build an impact-over-time curve that justifies a maximum tolerable period of disruption.
You will be able to run structured interviews with process owners that produce evidence rather than reassurance.
You will be able to derive recovery priorities and dependencies that shape continuity and recovery strategies.
You will be able to spot where an untested dependency or single supplier invalidates a stated recovery objective.

beginner.definition: A business impact analysis is a study of how much harm your company would suffer if a business process stopped working. It asks what each process needs, such as people, data and systems, and how the damage grows over time. The result guides recovery priorities.
beginner.whyItMatters: Most teams guess which system to fix first after an outage. Guessing puts effort in the wrong place and keeps the important work offline longer. A business impact analysis replaces opinion with evidence from the people who run each process. It also gives you numbers, so leaders can decide what recovery speed is worth paying for.
howItWorks: Start with the products and services your company sells, not with a list of servers.
Break each product into the business processes that deliver it to customers.
Ask the owner of each process what people, data, systems and suppliers it depends on.
Estimate the harm caused by an outage of one hour, one day and one week.
Compare those costs to find how long each process may safely stay offline.
Use the answers to set recovery orders and to check them with the business.
beginner.example: Think of a hospital. If the pharmacy system goes down, nurses can write paper orders for a short time. After a few hours, mistakes become dangerous and patients wait longer. So the pharmacy system is ranked as urgent, while the staff canteen till can wait until tomorrow. A business impact analysis is the conversation that produces those rankings before anything breaks, using patient safety and delay as the measure.
takeaways: Start from business processes, not from a list of technical assets.
Impact grows with time, so measure harm at several points during an outage.
Process owners must give the input, or the numbers will be guesses.

exercises.title: Business Impact Analysis - EASY
exercises.summary: Recall and recognition: definitions, one clear answer, single-step questions.

exercises.title: Business Impact Analysis - MEDIUM
exercises.summary: Application: read a short log or alert and choose the correct next step.

exercises.title: Business Impact Analysis - HARD
exercises.summary: Analysis: a multi-step scenario with distractors, evidence to weigh, and a reason to give.

exercises.title: Business Impact Analysis - EXTREMELY HARD
exercises.summary: Synthesis under pressure: incomplete evidence, competing priorities, and a decision you must defend.
